newsitem.title: JAPAN: FOCUS-Matsushita wants European TV stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Matsushita wants European TV stake.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd said on Thursday it was stepping up efforts to tap into the potentially lucrative digital broadcasting industry, joining rival Sony Corp's move to take stakes in European broadcasters.

Matsushita said the company was in talks with many European broadcasting operators over taking possible stakes, including British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc (BSkyB) set up by media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.

Asked whether Matsushita was talking with the BSkyB group over participation in the company, Seinosuke Kuraku, director in charge of the company's European division, said: "We are talking to everyone (on participation)... BSkyB could be a candidate."

Kuraku added Matsushita's was seeking a broadcasting partner in each area of the European market and BSkyB was one candidate. A spokesman later confirmed he was referring to the possibility of taking equity positions.

Matsushita, one of the biggest electronic and media groups in the world with brand names such as Panasonic, is mainly interested in getting its television hardware into people's homes and sees an equity stake as the best way to get leverage in the competitive market.
The broadcasting industry, which is switching to digital from analogue technology and rapidly replacing equipment, has become the hottest sector for consumer electronics makers.

Japan recently decided to launch terrestrial digital broadcasting as early as the year 2000, and analysts estimate that Japan's five terrestrial broadcasting stations, including their group firms, would spend about 1 trillion yen ($8.13 billion) to replace their studio-use equipment by 2000.
"Sony and of course Matsushita would be very serious in the broadcasting business over the next few years," said Tadashi Nishi, senior analyst at the Sakura Institute of Research.
Matsushita currently holds a 15 percent stake in DirecTV Japan, along with Mitsubishi Corp , Mitsubishi Electronic Corp and U.S. company Hughes Electronics Corp .
DirectTV will start beaming 100 channels later this year when it launches digital satellite broadcasting in Japan.

Matsushita's rival Sony Corp is still negotiating a share in Japan Sky Broadcasting (JSKyB) with News Corp and Japan's Softbank Corp. The company is scheduled to start beaming 12 channels into Japan this month.

Demand for digital broadcasting equipment is even greater in the European market. Britain, for instance, will launch digital cable television, digital satellite broadcasting and digital terrestrial broadcasting services in early 1998.
Matsushita said it had reorganised and strengthened its European broadcast operations this week with the creation of a new pan-European group, Panasonic Broadcast Europe.
The new organisation is responsible for sales and support activities for broadcasters and professional video users through all of Europe, Matsushita said.

Within three years, Matsushita targets annual European sales of 250 million marks ($149.6 million) of broadcasting equipment, such as portable professional video cameras. ($1=123 yen) ($ = 1.671 German Marks)
